method: Luminance is luminous intensity per unit of projected area, measured in candela per square metre, the unit the display industry calls the nit. Every listed unit is reduced to candela per square metre by one exact or definitional factor: the nit is 1, the kilonit 1,000 and the millinit 0.001; the stilb is one candela per square centimetre, 10,000 cd/m²; one candela per square foot is 1/0.09290304 = 10.76391041670972 cd/m² because a square foot is 0.3048 m squared; the foot-lambert is one candela per square foot divided by pi, 3.426259099635391 cd/m²; the lambert is one candela per square centimetre divided by pi, 3183.098861837907 cd/m²; and the apostilb is one candela per square metre divided by pi, 0.318309886183791 cd/m². A conversion multiplies by the source factor and divides by the target factor, so every ordered pair round trips. Input is trimmed and must be a plain decimal, optionally with grouped thousands; a leading decimal point is accepted, exponent form is refused, and a negative value or a base value above 10,000,000,000 cd/m² is rejected with the reason. Results carry six significant digits with trailing zeros trimmed and thousands grouped, and magnitudes outside 1e-6 to 1e12 switch to exponential form. The reference table lists rounded order-of-magnitude surface luminances, not specifications; the page states separately that luminance is not illuminance in lux and that a display's quoted nits are a small-area peak figure. Everything runs in the browser; nothing is uploaded, stored or sent anywhere.
